The Salinas hyperspectral dataset is a 512 x 217 pixel image with 204 spectral bands.
The Salinas dataset contains 16 identified ground truth classes and a total of 54,129 labeled samples.
PCA is a linear dimensionality reduction technique that uses an orthogonal transformation to convert high-dimensional data into linearly uncorrelated principal components.
LPP is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction technique that builds a graph incorporating the neighborhood information of the data set and computes a transformation matrix to preserve local structure.
Kernel PCA is a nonlinear extension of PCA that first maps the data to a higher-dimensional feature space using a kernel function before applying PCA.
DRR tries to remove redundant information in PCA components by predicting each coefficient through multivariate regression and retaining the non-predictable residual information.
At 5 dimensions, PCA and MDS achieve the highest classification accuracy of 94.87% on the Salinas dataset.
At 30 dimensions, DRR achieves a classification accuracy of 87.12%, outperforming PCA (86.37%), LPP (84.88%), and Kernel PCA (51.82%).
Dimensionality reduction is crucial for hyperspectral image classification to remove redundant and misleading information while preserving useful information.
The high dimensionality of hyperspectral data increases the computational burden and can negatively impact classification accuracy if not addressed.
Nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques like LPP and Kernel PCA can better capture the complicated spatial structure of high-dimensional hyperspectral features compared to linear PCA.
DRR aims to further improve upon PCA by nonlinearly removing the residual redundant information still present in the PCA components.
The experimental results on the Salinas dataset demonstrate the performance of different dimensionality reduction techniques at various dimensionality levels.
Choosing the appropriate dimensionality reduction method and dimensionality level is important for achieving high classification accuracy on hyperspectral image data.
The paper provides a comprehensive overview of common dimensionality reduction techniques and their application to hyperspectral image classification.
